R0.72F then uses regularly varying initial-layer weights to separate the \(1/3\) threshold of selected-root and the \(1/2\) threshold of Leray payment, and select the critical-log minimum boundary. R0.72G uses phase gauge, target row identity and Rolle–BV reduction on exact real one-carrier lattice to prove that the complete root mass is exactly logarithmic, and obtain critical-log complete-root sharp saturation. R0.72H proves that the number of carriers in the mixed row is independent of moment-resolved payment in the finite conjugate paired multi-carrier system; the all-odd Rudin–Shapiro family excludes the action-only version and makes the carrier powers encoded by the moment reach the same order. R0.72I proves that the separated \(B_AQ_*\) positive terms cannot be physically absorbed item by item, while using joint exposure and odd-carrier parity to prove the true complete ledger uniform attenuation. R0.72J completes the binary classification of gcd-reduced Cayley graph, distinguishes odd cycle and triangle return, and proves that common-band coherent mixed-parity cubic still decays after physical normalization. R0.72K closes the complete complex-target ledger by root-by-root gap norming direction, and proves that its common-band physical normalization ratio is still uniformly attenuated. R0.72L retains the actual enstrophy contrast and critical-log action, closing the moderate strong-coupling window that grows with \(R\); the upper edge of the window only decays in the little-o sub-interval for \(O(1)\). R0.72M accurately calculates the scalar action danger window and proves the Bessel action-poor benchmark and sharp logarithmic cubic law on a complete one-carrier zero-diffusion chain. R0.72N excludes the action-poor route that declares launch on the complete dissipative chain, and launches the local corollary \(\mathcal C_{\rm diss}\lesssim a^2\sqrt\sigma\) by Coble–He time-varying shear attenuation. R0.72O Backfill the physical ledger with this cubic to obtain the \(\varepsilon^{11/6}\) numerator and \(R^{4/3}L_{R,\varepsilon}^2\) window; multi-carrier conditions are only true under the assumption of full-superposition ED with unified constants.
